soundness_flags.label: ass:binary-observed
soundness_flags.one_line: Full binary observed support is a deliberate restricted subclass, not the standard positive-discrete selected-SCM condition supported by the cited discrete-settings paper; retag it novel and justify its scope, or lift the result to arbitrary finite observed alphabets.

soundness_flags.label: thm:complete-characterization
soundness_flags.one_line: The theorem formally ranges only over the newly defined binary subclass but says it strictly strengthens Chen--Mooij on their positive-discrete setting; either prove the full finite-discrete extension or state the binary-subclass contribution without that comparison.

soundness_flags.label: thm:formula-certificate-complexity
soundness_flags.one_line: An exact population law Pobs has no stated finite encoding or oracle model, so bit complexity for FC(PAG;Y,X,C,Pobs) is undefined; make FC graph/query-to-symbolic-output, or specify the representation and cost of Pobs evaluation.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: sIDP is sound and complete for unconditional selected kernels on COPAGs; the authors state that sCIDP soundness follows directly but leave its completeness and an appropriate conditional Hedge analogue to future work.
Algorithm 2/CIDP is complete for identifying conditional effects from a PAG without selection, and the associated calculus plus probability manipulations is complete for that task.
IDP is complete for unconditional causal-effect identification from a PAG and the paper derives a represented-MAG/forest nonidentifiability characterization.
The note says the classical hedge criterion is incorrect as stated while a hedge arises whenever the ID input distribution is not identified.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(547), 2024
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives a general method for causal questions with discrete data via polynomial programming; it does not present full binary observed support as the standard positive-discrete selected-SCM condition.
The paper studies graphical positivity conditions that license identification formulas without strict positivity, including post-hoc, do-calculus, Q-decomposition, and algorithmic approaches.
The work defines verification of a supplied observational formula as a problem complementary to identification and states that sound and complete identification alone does not solve verification.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Either extend the residual-forest and rational-witness construction to arbitrary finite observed alphabets or explicitly recast the paper as a binary selected-COPAG completeness theorem and remove claims of resolving Chen--Mooij's whole positive-discrete setting.

Specify a finite graph/query input model for FC and make formula evaluation against Pobs an explicitly separate oracle or rational-table task; then state the claimed output-sensitive bound in that model.

Add a theorem-level transfer or regression result showing exactly which sCIDP legal exchange sequences Branch-sCIDP adds beyond the published schedule and proving the S=emptyset reduction before pursuing the converse.

recommended_next_step: Revise the binary-scope comparison and computational input model, then advance the denominator-locked extraction OEQ to Stage 0 as the genuine field-tier kernel.
